task:
Merge keys bypass the alias limit, so a crafted document can exhaust the stack.

Take src = '&A { <<: *A, B: b }\n' and doc = parseDocument(src, { merge: true }). doc.errors and doc.warnings stay empty. doc.toJS() today fails with 'Maximum call stack size exceeded'. It must instead throw a ReferenceError with the message 'Excessive alias count indicates a resource exhaustion attack'. doc.toJS({ maxAliasCount: 0 }), doc.toJS({ maxAliasCount: 1 }) and doc.toJS({ maxAliasCount: 2 }) must each throw ReferenceError too. String(doc) must still equal src.

A merge through an alias must count as an alias use, like any other alias.

Merge pair built from a map alias. Start with parseDocument('[{ a: A }, { b: B }]', { merge: true }), and call the two maps a and b. Give a the anchor AA with an alias, and run b.set(doc.createPair('<<', alias)). doc.toJS() must match [{ a: 'A' }, { a: 'A', b: 'B' }]. doc.toJS({ maxAliasCount: 0 }) must throw ReferenceError. String(doc) must be '[ &AA { a: A }, { b: B, <<: *AA } ]\n'.

Merge pair built from an alias to a sequence of aliases. Start with parseDocument('[{ a: A }, [], { b: B }]', { merge: true }), and call the items a, seq and b. Set seq.anchor = 'SEQ', run seq.push(doc.createAlias(a, 'AA')), and run b.set(doc.createPair('<<', doc.createAlias(seq))). doc.toJS() must match [{ a: 'A' }, [{ a: 'A' }], { a: 'A', b: 'B' }]. doc.toJS({ maxAliasCount: 0 }) must throw ReferenceError. String(doc) must be '[ &AA { a: A }, &SEQ [ *AA ], { b: B, <<: *SEQ } ]\n'.

Everything else must keep working, including the resolved values of ordinary aliases and merges within the limit.
